name: Spindler Broodmother

facts.text: Level 81, 100,000 health. One or two newly-born spindlers hatch every few seconds while she fights.
When she dies, 20-25 underdeveloped spindlers burst from her body.
She mesmerises a random target every 20-30 seconds; her teleport is off for bot raids.
The Hibernian epic raid wiped at her once on 2026-11-05 (build 8d7baa3).

story:
The spindlers of Galladoria all come from one mother, and she has never stopped. The Broodmother is bloated past moving far, a sac of eggs on legs, and she does not need to hunt: the hollow brings her food. While she fights the young drop from her one by one and run at whoever is nearest. She lulls the strongest foe to stillness with a slow sway, as she lulls her eggs. And at the end, when her body fails, she gives the hollow everything she was still carrying, all at once. Raiders who celebrate her death too early have a short celebration.

Every spindler in Galladoria is her child, and she has never stopped. The Sylvan think she came into the hollow as an ordinary cave-spinner, small and quick, and that the sap made her into a mother and nothing else. She is bloated past moving far now, a sac of eggs on legs, and she does not hunt: the hollow brings her food, and her children bring her more.

While she fights the young drop from her one or two at a time, newly born and already hungry, and run at whoever is nearest. With a slow sway of her body she lulls her strongest foe into stillness, as she lulls her eggs. The first Living Server realm raid that came to her lost to her once, and had to be rescued by a band of the realm's best. And at the end, when her body fails, she does the last thing a mother can do. She gives the hollow everything she was still carrying, twenty or more half-formed young spilling out of her at once to avenge her. Raiders who cheer her death too early have a very short celebration.

She was a little cave-spinner of Domnann, made by the sap into nothing but a mother; the lurikeen Pádraigín of Howth, sole survivor of the first six, taught the realm to prepare for her death before striking her.
legend: Kill the hatchlings as they drop, steadily, and never forget the last part: when she dies twenty or more young spill out of her at once. Healers ready, AoE casters stacked on her corpse before the killing blow. Break the mezz on whoever she lulls. Stack the AoE casters behind the tank before the last tenth of her health, with healers ready on the melee. When she bursts, everything dies in the first two volleys or not at all. Superstition says never kill her while standing on an egg sac. Nobody remembers why; everybody steps off one when she gets low.

chapters.title: A Cave-Spinner of Domnann
chapters.text:
The spindlers of Hy Brasil were small things once, the Sylvan say: cave-spinners, quick and clever, that lived in the dry caves under the hills of Domnann and ate the moths that came in at dusk. Sylvan children kept them, the way children of other realms keep crickets, in little cages of woven reed. The children of Domnann still sing a rhyme about them, about a spinner who spun a bridge across a well, and the rhyme is older than the hollow.

One of them went down. The Sylvan do not know which, or when, but they know where, because the brood chamber in the south-western galleries of Galladoria lies directly below the old spinner caves of Domnann, a long way down. The sap of the hollow ran over her. It did to her what it does to everything that drinks it: it made her into one thing and nothing else. The Olcasar became hatred; the Uaimh became digging; the cave-spinner became a mother.

She is bloated past moving far now, a sac of eggs on legs as big as a cart, and she does not hunt. The hollow brings her food, and her children bring her more. Every spindler in Galladoria is hers. The realm's raiders who have fought in the galleries have killed thousands of them, and not one has been anything but her child. The rhyme ends with the spinner's bridge holding a child who fell, which is why Sylvan mothers stopped singing the last verse after the hollow came.

chapters.title: Newly Born
chapters.text:
While she fights, her young drop from her one or two at a time, newly born and already hungry, every few breaths. They run at whoever is nearest. The realm's fighters learned to kill them steadily, as they come, because a raid that ignores them for the mother finds itself standing in a crowd of them, each a little stronger than the last. With a slow sway of her great body she lulls her strongest foe into stillness, as she lulls her eggs, and the raid's menders learned to break the lull on whoever she chose. In the oldest fights she could also pull a raider across her chamber to her, as a spider draws in a line; she does not do that now.

The first Hibernians to fight her were not a raid at all. They were a band of six from Howth, led by a lurikeen named Pádraigín, who had heard that the brood chamber was the richest hunting in the hollow and went down to see. They killed the mother and stood over her body congratulating each other, and Pádraigín, the only one who came home, said afterward that the body moved under their feet like a sack of grain being poured. The five who died with her were Sylvan and Hibernian both, and Pádraigín carried their names to Domnann herself. She went back down the next season with forty, and they cheered nothing until the floor was still. Pádraigín kept their names on a cord at her belt for the rest of her life.

chapters.title: The Last Gift
chapters.text:
At the end, when her body fails, the Broodmother does the last thing a mother can do. She gives the hollow everything she was still carrying, twenty or more half-formed young spilling out of her at once, underdeveloped and furious, to avenge her. That is what killed Pádraigín's five, and it is the reason every Hibernian raid now prepares for her death before it ever strikes her: the casters of many targets stand behind the tank before her last tenth, the menders ready, and the young die in the first two volleys or not at all.

The Hibernian raid that went down not long ago, in the realm's current seasons, learned the lesson again. It reached her chamber tired, cheered her death, and was overwhelmed by the brood, and the realm had to send its best fighters down after it to bring the survivors out. Raid leaders since have told the story at every briefing before the brood chamber, and Pádraigín's name with it.

The Sylvan say a superstition grew up among the realm's raiders after that night, which they find touching: that you must never kill her while standing on one of her egg-sacs. Nobody remembers why. Everyone steps off one when she gets low. The Sylvan think it is the realm learning, in its own way, to respect a mother. Pádraigín's own rule, first said at that briefing, is still the one raid leaders use: do not cheer until the floor is still. The realm learned it the same way twice.

chapters.title: The Lullaby
chapters.text:
The Sylvan do not hate the Broodmother as they hate the other things in the hollow. They pity her. She was a cave-spinner, quick and clever, and the sap took everything she was except the part that makes more of herself. When the news comes up from Galladoria that the realm has killed her, the mothers of Domnann sing a lullaby, the old one about the spinner and the well, and they sing it not for her but for the ones that never hatched.

The druids of Tir na Nog have a harder view, and say so: that every spindler that reaches the upper galleries is a danger to the isle, and that the brood chamber lies directly under the spinner caves of Domnann, and that if her children ever dig upward they will find themselves at home. The Sylvan do not dispute it. They have stopped letting their children keep spinners in reed cages. Lisín said it was the saddest thing the hollow ever did to Domnann, to take away a children's game.

She always returns. A new mother, the Sylvan think, or the same one, grown again from an egg her last brood left behind. The realm's raids keep going down, and Pádraigín, who became a raid leader herself in time, used to say that she had killed the Broodmother more times than any Hibernian living, and that every time she stepped off the egg-sacs first. She is buried in Domnann, at her own wish, beside the spinner caves.
